issues.legal_issue: The government is a necessary party to compensation-objection proceedings and must receive individual notice of the objections and hearing through the prescribed recipient.
material_facts: An intermediary objected to the draft compensation assessment rolls and sought higher compensation.
The government, which was required to pay the compensation, was not joined or given notice of the objections or hearing.
The general Gazette notice was published, but no notice was sent to the District Collector or another authority nominated by the Collector.
issues.conclusion: The government was required to be joined as a party and was entitled to specific notice; the Gazette notice alone did not serve it, and the proceedings were prima facie not binding on it.
issues.legal_principle: Under sections 343, 46 and 47 of the Uttar Pradesh Zamindari Abolition and Land Reforms Act, 1950, the government must be joined in proceedings under the relevant chapters and receive notice through the Collector or an authority nominated by the Collector. The statutory definition of persons interested is not exhaustive; the government’s obligation to pay compensation gives it an interest in the proceeding. Deeming the government a party permits it to participate without first applying to be joined, but does not dispense with joining it or giving it notice.

rule.if: compensation_assessment_objection and government_must_pay_compensation and objection_seeks_changed_assessment and government_not_joined and government_not_individually_notified

predicates.compensation_assessment_objection: The proceeding concerned an objection to an assessment of compensation.
predicates.government_must_pay_compensation: The government was responsible for paying the compensation at issue.
predicates.objection_seeks_changed_assessment: A party objected to the assessment and sought a change in the amount of compensation.
predicates.government_not_joined: The government was not joined as a party to the objection proceeding.
predicates.government_not_individually_notified: No individual notice of the objection or hearing was sent to the government through its designated recipient.

issues.definition: When an objection seeks to change compensation payable by the government and the government is neither joined nor individually notified, the objection proceeding does not bind the government.

issues.legal_issue: A tribunal may consider reopening a proceeding decided without notice to a necessary party, and the tribunal must decide whether reopening is warranted.
material_facts: The government was not given notice of an intermediary’s objections or of the hearing on them.
After learning of the enhanced compensation assessment, the government applied to have the objection proceedings reopened.
The Compensation Officer had not yet decided whether to reopen the proceedings.
issues.conclusion: The government was entitled to ask for reopening, and the Compensation Officer had jurisdiction to decide whether to reopen; the Supreme Court did not itself direct that the proceedings be reopened.
issues.legal_principle: A court or tribunal may reopen a proceeding that went forward without notice to a necessary party, because a decision reached behind that party’s back is not binding on it. This is distinct from reopening an assessment merely for correction or review. The Court referred to section 343 of the Act, the use of the Code of Civil Procedure under section 48, and the inherent power under section 151 of that Code; the Compensation Officer must decide the reopening application in the first instance.

predicates.compensation_assessment_objection: The proceeding concerned an objection to an assessment of compensation.
predicates.necessary_party_not_notified: A party necessary to the objection proceeding received no notice of it.
predicates.reopening_application_pending: A party applied to the officer to reopen the proceeding, and the application remained undecided.

issues.definition: If a necessary party received no notice in a compensation-objection proceeding and an application to reopen remains pending, the officer may decide whether to reopen it.

issues.legal_issue: A writ of prohibition is premature when the officer has jurisdiction to consider a pending application to reopen and has not yet decided whether to reopen the proceeding.
material_facts: The government had applied to the Compensation Officer to reopen the objection proceedings because it had not received notice.
The Compensation Officer had not yet decided whether reopening was warranted.
The High Court issued a writ prohibiting the officer from proceeding with the government’s applications.
issues.conclusion: The High Court erred in issuing a writ of prohibition; the Compensation Officer had jurisdiction to consider the reopening applications, and the prohibition was dissolved.
issues.legal_principle: Whether the officer may proceed to reopen the underlying matter must be considered after the officer has addressed the reopening application. A writ of prohibition is not warranted merely because a party disputes the officer’s jurisdiction before the officer has made that determination.

predicates.prohibition_sought_against_pending_reope: A party sought a writ prohibiting an officer from acting on an application to reopen a proceeding.
predicates.officer_has_jurisdiction_to_consider_reo: The officer had jurisdiction to consider whether the proceeding should be reopened.
predicates.officer_has_not_decided_whether_to_reope: The officer had not yet decided whether to reopen the proceeding.

issues.definition: When an officer with jurisdiction to consider reopening has not yet decided the pending application, a writ prohibiting the officer from acting on it is premature.

issues.legal_issue: A claim of privilege over requested government documents must be reconsidered when it has not been properly raised and supported.
material_facts: The intermediary requested discovery and production of government documents said to show that the government knew of or participated in the objection proceedings.
The government claimed privilege over the documents, and the Compensation Officer allowed the claim.
The Supreme Court maintained the order quashing the decision on the privilege claim and directed that the claim be properly raised and decided.
issues.conclusion: The privilege claim had not been properly raised and had to be reconsidered after appropriate affidavits from the heads of the departments concerned, applying the cited decisions.
issues.legal_principle: The claim of privilege must be examined in accordance with law after appropriate affidavits are filed by the heads of the departments concerned. The Court directed the Compensation Officer to consider the claim in light of The State of Punjab v. Sodhi Sukhdev Singh and Amar Chand Butail v. Union of India and Others.

rule.if: compensation_assessment_objection and documents_requested_from_government and government_claimed_privilege and privilege_claim_not_properly_supported

predicates.compensation_assessment_objection: The proceeding concerned an objection to an assessment of compensation.
predicates.documents_requested_from_government: A party requested government documents relevant to the proceeding.
predicates.government_claimed_privilege: The government asserted privilege over the requested documents.
predicates.privilege_claim_not_properly_supported: The privilege claim had not been properly raised and supported by appropriate affidavits from the responsible department heads.

issues.definition: When the government claims privilege over requested documents in a compensation-objection proceeding but has not properly supported that claim, the claim must be reconsidered with proper support.
